title: Writing a model in R
text: set names dimension lists values.
code: techs   <- c("coal", "gas", "wind") regions <- c("north", "south")  sets <- list(   tech   = new_set("tech",   desc = "generation technologies", data = techs),   region = new_set("region", desc = "model regions",           data = regions) ) sets$tech #> <AST set> tech

title: Writing a model in R
text: mapping table tuples one sets. Mappings serve domains: indexed variable equation exists exactly tuples domain mapping, sparse models stay sparse. every technology may built every region, domain full grid.
code: tuples <- expand.grid(tech = techs, region = regions, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)  mappings <- list(   mTR = new_mapping("mTR", desc = "technology x region pairs",                     dims = c("tech", "region"), data = tuples),   mR  = new_mapping("mR",  desc = "regions",                     dims = "region", data = data.frame(region = regions)) ) mappings$mTR$data #>   tech region #> 1 coal  north #> 2  gas  north #> 3 wind  north #> 4 coal  south #> 5  gas  south #> 6 wind  south

title: Writing a model in R
text: parameter declares dimensions carries data frame one column per dimension plus value.
code: parameters <- list(   pCapCost = new_parameter("pCapCost", desc = "annualised capacity cost, EUR/kW",     dims = "tech",     data = data.frame(tech = techs, value = c(120, 70, 90))),   pVarCost = new_parameter("pVarCost", desc = "variable cost, EUR/MWh",     dims = "tech",     data = data.frame(tech = techs, value = c(30, 55, 0))),   pAvail = new_parameter("pAvail", desc = "availability factor",     dims = c("tech", "region"),     data = transform(tuples, value = c(0.85, 0.85, 0.90, 0.90, 0.35, 0.25))),   pDemand = new_parameter("pDemand", desc = "annual demand, MWh",     dims = "region",     data = data.frame(region = regions, value = c(1000, 600))) ) parameters$pAvail #> <AST parameter> pAvail #>   dims:  [tech,region]

title: Writing a model in R
text: Variables declare dimensions, domain mapping, type bounds. scalar variable dims = character(0).
code: variables <- list(   vCap = new_variable("vCap", desc = "installed capacity, kW",                       dims = c("tech", "region"), domain = "mTR",                       vtype = "positive", bounds = list(lo = 0)),   vGen = new_variable("vGen", desc = "generation, MWh",                       dims = c("tech", "region"), domain = "mTR",                       vtype = "positive", bounds = list(lo = 0)),   vCost = new_variable("vCost", desc = "total system cost, EUR",                        dims = character(0)) )

title: Writing a model in R
text: Inside equation, symbols referenced rather declared: ast_variable() ast_parameter() take name index symbols, given ast_dims(). ast_expression() combines two nodes operator, ast_sum() sums expression index symbols. Rendering method node, expression can checked used:
code: gen   <- ast_variable("vGen", dims = ast_dims("tech", "region")) avail <- ast_parameter("pAvail", dims = ast_dims("tech", "region")) cap   <- ast_variable("vCap", dims = ast_dims("tech", "region"))  limit <- ast_expression("*", avail, cap) node_type(limit) #> [1] "expression" limit #> <AST expression> * #>   lhs : #> <AST parameter> pAvail #>   dims:  [tech,region]  #>   rhs: #> <AST variable> vCap #>   dims:  [tech,region] as_gams(limit) #> [1] "pAvail[tech,region] * vCap[tech,region]" as_latex(limit) #> [1] "\\mathsf{pAvail}_{\\texttt{tech},\\texttt{region}}  \\cdot  \\bm{\\mathit{vCap}}_{\\texttt{tech},\\texttt{region}}"

title: Writing a model in R
text: new_model() assembles components. objective declared equation defines , variable defines sense. Every constructor validates node AST schema built (ast_schema() lists node types fields), malformed node refused written. validate() checks assembled model: every symbol referenced equation must declared, matching dimensions. text backends write indexed expressions short iterator names (sum{t tech} MathProg, t tech Julia). model built R none add_index_aliases() derives set names:
code: toy <- new_model(   name = "toy", desc = "two-region capacity expansion",   sets = sets, mappings = mappings, parameters = parameters,   variables = variables,   equations = list(eqCapLim = eqCapLim, eqDemand = eqDemand, eqCost = eqCost),   objectives = list(list(equation = "eqCost", variable = "vCost",                          sense = "minimize")) ) toy #> Model: toy #> Description: two-region capacity expansion #> Sets:  2  #> Mappings:  2  #> Aliases:  0  #> Parameters:  4  #> Variables:  3  #> Equations:  3 v <- validate(toy) v$valid #> [1] TRUE toy <- add_index_aliases(toy) unlist(toy$index_aliases) #>   tech region  #>    "h"    "r"

title: Writing a model in R
text: matrix route needs external software: model_to_lp() builds constraint matrix equations data, solve_highs() passes HiGHS solver (‘highs’ package). file routes render model external solver: write_gmpl() GLPK, write_jump() Julia write_pyomo() Python; vignette("multimod") lists solve_*() counterparts.
code: lp <- model_to_lp(toy) dim(lp$A) #> [1]  9 13 r <- solve_highs(toy, attach = FALSE) r$objective #> [1] 198000 head(r$primal[r$primal$value > 0, ], 10) #>        j symbol     i1     i2    lo    up      vtype       value reduced_cost #>    <int> <char> <char> <char> <num> <num>     <char>       <num>        <num> #> 1:     3   vCap   wind  north     0   Inf   positive   1111.1111            0 #> 2:     4   vCap   coal  south     0   Inf   positive    666.6667            0 #> 3:     9   vGen   wind  north     0   Inf   positive   1000.0000            0 #> 4:    10   vGen   coal  south     0   Inf   positive    600.0000            0 #> 5:    13  vCost   <NA>   <NA>  -Inf   Inf continuous 198000.0000            0 mod_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".mod") write_gmpl(toy, file = mod_file) cat(head(readLines(mod_file), 12), sep = "\n") #> # Model: toy #> # two-region capacity expansion #>  #> set tech;  # generation technologies #> set region;  # model regions #>  #>  #> set _IF_;  # Singleton set for GAMS $ operator emulation #>  #> set mTR dimen 2;  # technology x region pairs #> set mR dimen 1;  # regions

title: Two models from the field
text: OSeMOSYS, Open Source Energy Modelling System, written GNU MathProg. repository OSeMOSYS/OSeMOSYS_GNU_MathProg (Apache License 2.0, copyright 2010-2015 OSeMOSYS Forum steering committee) holds model file src/osemosys.txt UTOPIA test case tests/utopia.txt. Nothing bundled multimod; section reads local clone whose path environment variable MULTIMOD_OSEMOSYS_DIR. reference result UTOPIA objective glpsol reports two files, 29446.86. Cite: Howells, M., Rogner, H., Strachan, N., Heaps, C., Huntington, H., Kypreos, S., Hughes, ., Silveira, S., DeCarolis, J., Bazilian, M. Roehrl, . (2011). OSeMOSYS: Open Source Energy Modeling System. introduction ethos, structure development. Energy Policy, 39(10), 5850-5870. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enpol.2011.06.033 reader returns 11 sets, 61 parameters, 68 variables 95 equations. Twenty-six parameters carry UTOPIA data; six formulas parameters (discount factors, capital recovery factor, annuity), rest take declared defaults, among parametric default, DiscountRateIdv defaulting DiscountRate[r].

title: Folding and trimming
text: Framework models energyRt written maximum flexibility: one generic set equations covers technologies, storage, trade, emissions , every parameter indexed every dimension ever vary (technology, commodity, region, year, timeslice). given scenario uses part : single-region model interregional trade, technologies efficiency every timeslice, features scenario use leave sets mappings empty, equations depend generate constraints. flexibility paid model-build time solver: data repeated across dimension inflates data files coefficient count, equations empty domains still processed. multimod offers two complementary transformations remove redundancy without changing optimum: Folding removes dimension parameter values constant across (data redundancy). Trimming marks sets, parameters, mappings, variables equations data instances, code generators skip (structural redundancy). reversible honoured every writer direct matrix route.

title: Export the bundled energyRt model as a solver workspace — export_model_source
text: dataset Name dataset export. Currently "energyrt". dir Directory path workspace. Created exist. format backend export: "gams", "gmpl", "jump", "pyomo", "" (default). overwrite Logical. TRUE, existing solver directories rewritten. Default FALSE: backend whose directory exists skipped. verbose Logical. TRUE, print progress messages. Default TRUE.

title: Export the bundled energyRt model as a solver workspace — export_model_source
text: Invisibly, character vector files written.

title: Export the bundled energyRt model as a solver workspace — export_model_source
text: workspace layout one every solve_*() function expects: model.rds, sets/, mappings/, parameters/: saved model data (CSV), written save_model(). solvers/gams/model.gms: GAMS source energyRt model. solvers/gmpl/model.mod data.dat: MathProg, run glpsol -m model.mod -d data.dat directory. solvers/jump/model.jl data.jl: JuMP, run julia model.jl. solvers/pyomo/model.py data.py: Pyomo, run python model.py. README.txt: provenance licence model.

Simple, robust, works everywhere Julia installed. juliacall: Uses JuliaCall package R-Julia integration. Allows bi-directional data transfer access Julia objects R. title: Julia source of the JuMP solution writer — write_jump_solution_code
code: # Julia source of the save_solution() helper embedded in generated model.jl cat(write_jump_solution_code()) #>  #> # Function to save solution values #> function save_solution(model, output_dir, data_format) #>     using Dates #>     using DataFrames #>     using CSV #>     using Arrow #>      #>     if !isdir(output_dir) #>         mkpath(output_dir) #>     end #>      #>     println("\nSaving solution to: ", output_dir) #>      #>     # Determine file extension #>     ext = data_format == "csv" ? ".csv" : ".arrow" #>      #>     # Save each variable #>     for (var_name, var_obj) in object_dict(model) #>         if !(var_obj isa AbstractArray{VariableRef}) #>             continue #>         end #>          #>         # Get variable values #>         var_vals = value.(var_obj) #>          #>         # Convert to DataFrame based on dimensions #>         if var_obj isa DenseAxisArray #>             # Get indices #>             indices = axes(var_obj) #>             n_dims = length(indices) #>              #>             if n_dims == 0 #>                 # Scalar variable #>                 df = DataFrame(value = [var_vals]) #>             else #>                 # Multi-dimensional variable #>                 idx_names = [Symbol("dim$i") for i in 1:n_dims] #>                 rows = [] #>                  #>                 for idx in Iterators.product(indices...) #>                     val = var_vals[idx...] #>                     if abs(val) > 1e-10  # Only save non-zero values #>                         push!(rows, (idx..., val)) #>                     end #>                 end #>                  #>                 if !isempty(rows) #>                     df = DataFrame(rows, vcat(idx_names, :value)) #>                 else #>                     df = DataFrame() #>                 end #>             end #>         else #>             # Default handling #>             df = DataFrame(value = [var_vals]) #>         end #>          #>         # Save to file #>         if !isempty(df) #>             var_dir = joinpath(output_dir, string(var_name)) #>             mkpath(var_dir) #>             out_file = joinpath(var_dir, "data" * ext) #>              #>             if ext == ".csv" #>                 CSV.write(out_file, df) #>             else #>                 Arrow.write(out_file, df) #>             end #>              #>             println("  Saved ", string(var_name), ": ", nrow(df), " values") #>         end #>     end #>      #>     println("Solution saved successfully\n") #> end #>  #> # Save solution after solving #> if termination_status(model) == MOI.OPTIMAL ||  #>    termination_status(model) == MOI.LOCALLY_SOLVED #>      #>     run_name = Dates.format(now(), "yyyy-mm-dd_HHMMSS") #>     solution_dir = joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "..", "solutions", run_name) #>     save_solution(model, solution_dir, DATA_FORMAT) #> end

Code testing inherits(x, "model") must use new names; models saved 0.0.1 must rebuilt. constructors validate node schema built, malformed node refused . options(multimod.validate = FALSE) disables check. arrow visNetwork suggested rather imported; functions need fail installation hint.

text: mm_equation() builds equation MathProg, GAMS JuMP text. read_gmpl() reads MathProg models data sections, computed parameters parametric defaults. parse_jump_equation() reads JuMP @constraint() statement. read_gams() read_gmpl() accept text well file paths. title: multimod 0.5.0
text: model_to_lp() assembles LP matrix directly model, including symbols declared sets, equation conditions, lags leads, formula parameters. solve_highs() solves assembled LP R returns primal dual values; mm_session() keeps matrix repeated solves. write_mps() writes LP MPS, optional presolve (lp_presolve()) eliminates proportional columns; solve_mps() solves MPS file read_mps_solution(), read_highs_solution(), read_cuopt_solution() read_solver_solution() read solutions back. check_matrix_numbers() reports coefficient range assembled LP. solve_gmpl(), solve_jump() solve_pyomo() run generated code load solution model.
